subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw officially document an advanced public `wss://` mobile-pairing recipe with split admin/mobile hostnames and no browser SSO gate on the mobile WebSocket hostname, alongside Tailscale Serve as the default recommendation?
rationale: The requested docs define supported public-exposure security posture for mobile setup-code bootstrap, trusted proxies, edge identity gates, and operator/browser surfaces, which automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Document default plus advanced recipe
options.body: Publish Tailscale Serve as the recommended remote path and add a clearly labeled advanced public `wss://` recipe with split hostnames, OpenClaw-native mobile auth, trusted proxy setup, Settings paste fallback, and release caveats.

options.title: Keep Tailscale-first only
options.body: Keep public docs centered on Tailscale Serve and avoid blessing direct public mobile WebSocket exposure until the team has a stronger product/security posture for that deployment.

options.title: Defer until app flow ships broadly
options.body: Hold the docs decision until QR, onboarding paste, and route-selection fixes are confirmed in the App Store build and can be described as a supported in-product flow.

recommendation.title: Document default plus advanced recipe
recommendation.body: Publish Tailscale Serve as the recommended remote path and add a clearly labeled advanced public `wss://` recipe with split hostnames, OpenClaw-native mobile auth, trusted proxy setup, Settings paste fallback, and release caveats.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged route-selection work and adjacent mobile pairing history make this the best available owner signal for the product/security decision.
